args:
set -eu
umask 077
path=$1; cap=$2
fail() { printf '%s: %s\n' "$1" "$2" >&2; exit 1; }
lk_claim() {
  lk_c="$lk_lock/pid.claim.$$"
  mv "$lk_lock/pid" "$lk_c" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  if [ "$(cat "$lk_c" 2>/dev/null)" = "$1" ]; then
    lk_gone="$lk_lock.dead.$$"
    rm -rf "$lk_gone"
    mv "$lk_lock" "$lk_gone" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    rm -rf "$lk_gone" 2>/dev/null || :
    return 0
  fi
  mv "$lk_c" "$lk_lock/pid" 2>/dev/null || :
  return 1
}
lock() {
  lk_lock=$1; tries=0
  lk_token="$$ $(date +%s)"
  lk_stage="$lk_lock.$$"
  while :; do
    rm -rf "$lk_stage"
    mkdir "$lk_stage" || fail "$lk_stage" 'cannot create the lock directory'
    printf '%s\n' "$lk_token" > "$lk_stage/pid"
    if [ ! -e "$lk_lock" ] && mv "$lk_stage" "$lk_lock" 2>/dev/null && [ "$(cat "$lk_lock/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$lk_token" ]; then break; fi
    # mv onto a lock that appeared meanwhile moves the stage into it.
    rm -rf "$lk_stage" "$lk_lock/${lk_stage##*/}"
    tries=$((tries + 1))
    [ "$tries" -le 100 ] || fail "$lk_lock" 'lock held by another writer'
    holder=$(cat "$lk_lock/pid" 2>/dev/null) || holder=
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && { ! kill -0 "${holder%% *}" 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(find "$lk_lock/pid" -mmin +1 2>/dev/null)" ]; }; then
      lk_claim "$holder" || :
      continue
    fi
    sleep 0.05
  done
  trap 'lk_claim "$lk_token" || :' EXIT
  trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
}
case $path in /*) ;; *) path=./$path;; esac
dir=${path%/*}
[ -n "$dir" ] || dir=/
mkdir -p "$dir" || fail "$dir" 'cannot create the log directory'
lock "$path.lock"
if [ -f "$path" ]; then
  bytes=$(wc -c < "$path")
  bytes=$((bytes))
  if [ "$bytes" -gt "$cap" ]; then mv -f "$path" "$path.1"; fi
fi
# An append killed mid-row leaves a torn last line; the rows retried after it start on their own line.
if [ -s "$path" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c 1 "$path")" ]; then printf '\n' >> "$path"; fi
cat >> "$path"

set -eu
dir=$1; prefix=$2; suffix=$3; days=$4; keep=$5; self=$6
case $dir in /*) ;; *) dir=./$dir;; esac
[ -d "$dir" ] || exit 0
cd "$dir"
named() {
  case $1 in "$prefix"*"$suffix") ;; *) return 1;; esac
  id=${1#"$prefix"}; id=${id%"$suffix"}
  case $id in [0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]-[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]-[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]-[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]-[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]) ;; *) return 1;; esac
}
file() { [ -f "./$1" ] && ours "$1"; }
ours() { IFS= read -r first < "./$1" || return 1; case $first in '{"ts":"'*'","event":"'*) ;; *) return 1;; esac; }
# One find lists every entry past the age, a symlink by its own; old() looks a name up in it, so no process runs per file.
# An entry another session removes mid-listing makes find exit 1: the names it printed stand, the rest read as not old.
nl='
'
olds=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -mmin +$((days * 1440)) -print) || :
old() { case "$nl$olds$nl" in *"$nl./$1$nl"*) return 0;; esac; return 1; }
kept=1
ls -t . | while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ "$name" != "$self" ] && named "$name" && file "$name" || continue
  if [ "$kept" -lt "$keep" ] && ! old "$name"; then kept=$((kept + 1)); continue; fi
  rm -f "./$name" "./$name.1"
done
# A rotated half whose session file is gone goes by its own age.
ls . | while IFS= read -r name; do
  case $name in *.1) ;; *) continue;; esac
  base=${name%.1}
  [ "$base" != "$self" ] && named "$base" && [ ! -e "./$base" ] && file "$name" || continue
  if old "$name"; then rm -f "./$name"; fi
done

args.name: forward_compaction
args.description:
Hands off your context — at a milestone once your context is large, or when a forward-compaction nudge asks. Stores your handoff; at Claude Code's next compaction everything before this call is replaced by it plus recorded facts (the person's messages or your brief, your skills), and every message after this call is kept verbatim. Returns a receipt saying when it installs; a refusal names what to fix and stores nothing. Example: forward_compaction({"handoff": "## Objective
…
## Done
…
## Remaining
…
## Next
…", "load_files": []}). Exact old detail later → look_back.

handoff.description: Markdown, at most 20000 characters, with these level-2 headings, each followed by at least one line: ## Objective (what the work is for and what done means), ## Done (finished pieces, each with how it was verified), ## Remaining (every step left, in order), ## Next (the first concrete action after the wake). Optional: ## Blocked (what waits on whom), ## Findings (decisions with why, errors verbatim). Write it for yourself after a reset: the messages before this call will be gone.

load_files.description: Files carried whole into the new context, read when it installs. A file too big to carry is named in the wake as not carried, never cut.

args.name: look_back
args.description: Recover an exact detail — when you need an error text, code snippet, value, or what the user said from before your latest compaction. Searches only your own transcript’s part you no longer hold. Each call tells the person what you looked up. Returns numbered snippets or a whole entry; failures say why, no matches suggests other words. Example: {query:"connection refused"}.

query.description: Case-insensitive words; entries holding the most of them rank first, then newest. Double quotes keep a phrase whole; \" is a literal quote.

entry.description: Line number from a look_back result to fetch whole, before the latest compaction.
